#### 1. Usher syndrome type 1B  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360, Reactome:R-HSA-9662361, Reactome:R-HSA-2453902)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYO7A (HGNC:7606) —DISRUPTS→ inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000317); inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000317) —LEADS_TO→ hearing impairment (HP:0000365); inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000317) —LEADS_TO→ vestibular dysfunction (HP:0002401). Loss-of-function mutations in MYO7A disrupt the function of the stereocilia in inner ear hair cells, impairing mechanotransduction. This disruption leads to hearing impairment (ARNSHL2) and, when more severe or affecting other hair cell functions, can also cause vestibular dysfunction, characteristic of Usher syndrome type 1B.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in MYO7A that lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, or the absence of any MYO7A variants in individuals with these conditions. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD revealing a common pathogenic variant in MYO7A with an allele frequency > 0.01% would falsify its role as a rare disease gene.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared MYO7A mechanism provides a common therapeutic target for both ARNSHL2 and USH1B, potentially enabling gene therapy or small molecule approaches to restore MYO7A function and ameliorate hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction.
